incidents.symptom: First UI push passed all 166 remote tests but the Pages publish job was rejected before runner execution: the UI branch was not allowed by github-pages environment protection rules.
incidents.rootCause: The new Pages-only environment defaulted to a selected main branch rule. Preflight inspected Pages Source and workflow branch but did not verify the actual environment deployment branch rule.
incidents.resolution: Changed the existing Pages-only selected branch rule from main to the exact UI preview branch, keeping one branch and zero tags, with no environment secrets or variables and no Production change. Failed job rerun succeeded and the real public site opened with b82c400 metadata. Added an offline observation guard and eight negative/positive tests; corrected its initial nested-button-label parsing failure against the real snapshot.
incidents.prevention: Before publication inspect actual Pages Source, workflow source branch and Pages-only environment allowed branch. Keep Selected branches mode and reject widened or mismatched rules, credentials and tags. Treat saved-observation tests, actual remote deployment and live-site visits as separate evidence.

incidents.symptom: A slow authenticated message request completed with HTTP 201 after its session had been revoked by logout; expected HTTP 401 and no write. First core integration run: 18 PASS, 1 FAIL.
incidents.rootCause: Session was validated before awaiting the streamed request body and the cached actor was used after logout. Membership was checked but the session revocation was not rechecked at mutation time.
incidents.resolution: Added an authorized-body reader that revalidates the session after body completion for all authenticated JSON mutations. The exact delayed-body/logout attack now receives 401 and stores zero messages; 19/19 current core tests pass. Independent review pending.
incidents.prevention: Revalidate authentication after every asynchronous boundary before a state-changing operation; check membership and expected versions transactionally. Keep a real HTTP delayed-body/logout regression, not a mocked authorization result.

incidents.symptom: The same client message UUID with uppercase letters created a second message (HTTP 201); the negative idempotency test expected HTTP 422. Initial hardening run: 5 PASS, 1 FAIL.
incidents.rootCause: UUID validation accepted both cases while the SQLite idempotency key compared literal strings. One logical UUID could therefore have two keys.
incidents.resolution: Require canonical lowercase UUIDv4 throughout the protocol; native generated IDs already use that form. Preserve the database unique key and reject uppercase input before writing.
incidents.prevention: Use one canonical ID representation for all protocol inputs and exercise alternative encodings in idempotency regressions.

incidents.symptom: The new source-preservation test falsely failed on unchanged harness.yml because Windows checkout CRLF differed from the LF Git blob. First combined 33-test run: 32 PASS, 1 FAIL.
incidents.rootCause: The test compared raw working-tree strings with Git blob strings without applying Git checkout normalization.
incidents.resolution: Compare git hash-object --path with the baseline blob OID. This honors repository clean filters while still detecting source changes. Preserve prior incident objects separately by deep equality.
incidents.prevention: For Git source-preservation assertions compare canonical Git blobs instead of platform-specific checkout newlines; keep Linux CI and Windows local execution.

Root reproduced all three: 0/3 PASS.
incidents.rootCause: Recovery trusted a schema revision marker instead of the full schema, used a create-capable Store for backup paths, and committed seed accounts before writing their private credentials.
incidents.resolution: Reject missing backup/CLI server sources; validate complete tables, constraints, indexes, integrity and foreign keys before opening an existing database or creating a restore target; preflight and exclusively reserve private output and commit all account rows only after the credential write is synced, cleaning failed output and rolling back inserts.
incidents.prevention: Test wrong paths and corrupt/incomplete schema before reporting recovery success. Provisioning errors must leave a retryable database. Never silently repair an incompatible backup or claim an empty replacement is successful recovery.
